seoDescription: Join legendary producer Philippe Zdar as he demonstrates his unique approach to mixing guitars for the band Phoenix. This detailed tutorial showcases his philosophy on using outboard gear, including classic DBX and SSL compressors and the sought-after Helios equalizer, to shape guitar tone. Learn Zdar's techniques for creating space and texture through strategic panning, applying phasers and spring reverb, and blending different guitar parts. He also reveals a signature Phoenix technique for building tension using lo-fi drones.

chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.description: The video begins with a musical introduction featuring the track being mixed.

chapters.title: Selecting Compressors & EQs for Guitars
chapters.description: Philippe Zdar discusses his preference for using specific outboard gear, like the Helios EQ and SSL/DBX compressors, for mixing guitars.

chapters.title: Patching the Signal Chain
chapters.description: An instrumental segment shows the process of patching and configuring the outboard effects.

chapters.title: Creating Space with Panning & Effects
chapters.description: Zdar explains his crucial technique of panning guitars to create air and separation in the mix, then adds a phaser to one guitar.

chapters.title: Blending the Phaser Effect
chapters.description: He demonstrates how to blend a mono phaser effect with the direct guitar signal to add texture without widening the instrument's image.

chapters.title: The Phoenix Drone Technique for Tension
chapters.description: Zdar reveals a signature Phoenix technique of using subtle, lo-fi drones to add underlying stress and tension to a track.

chapters.title: The Value of Outboard Gear
chapters.description: He encourages producers to invest in even a few pieces of unique outboard hardware to develop a personal and distinct sound.

chapters.title: Demonstrating the 'Stress' Layer
chapters.description: The drone's effect is demonstrated by adding and removing it from the mix to show how it creates tension.

chapters.title: The Psychology of Mixing: Setup vs. Flow
chapters.description: Zdar shares his philosophy on separating the technical setup from the creative mixing process to maintain a state of creative flow.

summary:
## Core Mixing Philosophy

*   **Favorites for Instruments**: It's beneficial to have favorite pieces of gear (compressors, EQs) for specific instruments to quickly achieve a desired sound. The Helios EQ is a favorite for guitars due to its midrange character and slight distortion when pushed.
*   **Create a Unique Sound**: The ultimate goal is to create a unique sound that is personal to the artist and producer, a goal made easier by using select pieces of hardware.

## Key Techniques & Concepts

### Panning for Space

-   **Panning is a key** to creating a clear and spacious mix.
-   Even slight panning helps create "air" and separates elements. Avoid the temptation to stack everything on the extreme left and right sides.

### The Phoenix "Drone" Technique

-   A signature technique is to add subtle **drone layers** to create underlying tension and stress.
-   These drones are meant to be felt rather than heard distinctly.
-   This involves mixing **lo-fi sources** (like a Casio keyboard) with **hi-fi sounds** (like a CS-80 or Trident synth) within the same track.

> [!NOTE]
> Removing the drone layer reveals its impact, as a lot of the track's tension disappears with it. It serves a similar function to a tense film score.

### Blending Effects

-   Instead of using an effect as a 100% wet insert, blend it with the dry signal for more control.
-   To add texture without unwanted stereo widening, pan the effect return to the **exact same position** as the dry source signal.

## Gear & Workflow

### The Value of Outboard Gear

-   **Helios EQ**: Praised for its character on guitars, especially its midrange and the slight, pleasant distortion when driven.
-   **SSL Console Compressors (DBX-made)**: Very capable and can be used to mix entire songs effectively.

> [!TIP]
> Producers working "in the box" are encouraged to buy even one or two unique outboard pieces (e.g., a spring reverb, a delay pedal) to develop a signature sound that stands out. Expensive gear like an EMT 250 isn't necessary to start.

### Psychological Workflow

-   Separate the mixing process into two distinct mental states:
    1.  **Setup Phase**: The technical work of patching inserts and setting up the console. Acknowledge that this is not the "creative" part.
    2.  **Creative "Tripping" Phase**: The actual mixing and creative decision-making.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Psychologically separating these two phases helps avoid frustration and allows you to enter a state of creative flow when it's time to mix.
